summary: This resolution directs the House Oversight Committee chair to sue or intervene in federal court within 30 days to enforce a March 17, 2026 subpoena requiring Pamela Bondi to give deposition testimony on the Justice Department's handling of Jeffrey Epstein files and sex trafficking enforcement.

scores.thoughts: The resolution directs a House committee to enforce a subpoena through judicial proceedings. It contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any government expenditures or appropriations.
The resolution addresses subpoena enforcement related to an Epstein investigation and has no connection to tax policy, rates, or administration.
No provisions in the resolution relate to healthcare delivery, coverage, regulation, or funding.
The resolution has no bearing on firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa-related content appears in the resolution.
The resolution does not address reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No military, defense, or national security spending provisions are present.
The resolution contains nothing related to environmental regulation or climate policy.
No welfare, entitlement, or social services programs are mentioned.
The resolution has no education policy content.
The underlying investigation concerns sex trafficking enforcement, not drug decriminalization or enforcement.

While the subpoena relates to DOJ enforcement of sex trafficking laws, the resolution itself is strictly procedural (subpoena enforcement) and does not alter sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation policies.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions exist.
The resolution does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions touch on LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
Foreign aid is not mentioned or affected.
The resolution has no election administration or voting access content.
No technology regulation or data privacy measures are included.
Labor, union, or employment policy is absent.
The resolution does not engage religious liberty or anti-discrimination issues.
